title: Farm Real Estate Loans Note Terms: Prepayment of Principal and the Prepayment Fee
content:
Principal of a Farm Real Estate Loans mortgage may be prepaid in part or in full at any time.

## Terms

1. **Loan year.** The loan year is the 12-month period beginning on the closing date — or, after a conversion, the conversion date — or on an anniversary of it.
2. **Free allowance.** Prepayments in a loan year up to the product's free prepayment allowance percentage of the principal balance at the start of that loan year (the principal at the start of the loan year's first day), counting earlier prepayments of the same loan year net of returns, carry no fee.
3. **Fee on the excess.** The excess carries the fee percentage of the product's prepayment fee schedule entry for the current loan year, rounded to cents and booked as a prepayment fee pointing to the principal payment it is charged on.
4. **Payoffs.** Payoffs count as prepayments of the whole balance.
5. **Release proceeds and other amounts.** Release proceeds from a sale or farmstead split count toward the allowance and the fee; condemnation awards, scheduled installments and a rate conversion never carry a prepayment fee.
6. **No schedule.** A product with an empty schedule, and every loan year past the schedule's last entry, carries no fee.
7. **Effect on the schedule.** A prepayment shortens the schedule; the installment is unchanged until the next scheduled adjustment or conversion.

## How the excess is figured

The allowance still free is the start-of-year principal multiplied by the free allowance percentage, rounded to cents, less the prepayments already made in the loan year, never below zero. The chargeable part of a prepayment is the prepayment less the allowance still free, never below zero. The fee is the chargeable part multiplied by the schedule's fee percentage for the current loan year, rounded to cents.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)

A FarmLand 5-Year Adjustable Mortgage is in loan year 3; its principal at the start of that loan year was USD 800000.00 and USD 100000.00 has already been prepaid in the loan year. The member prepays a further USD 90000.00.

- Allowance: 20 percent of 800000.00 is 160000.00; less 100000.00 already prepaid, 60000.00 is still free.
- Chargeable part: 90000.00 less 60000.00 is 30000.00.
- Fee: the loan year 3 entry of that product is 2.0 percent; 2.0 percent of 30000.00 is USD 600.00.

| Amount | Prepayment fee? |
|---|---|
| prepayment within the allowance still free | no |
| excess over the allowance, in a loan year covered by the schedule | yes, at that year's fee percentage |
| release proceeds from a sale or farmstead split | counted toward the allowance and the fee |
| condemnation award | never |
| scheduled installment | never |
| rate conversion | never |
| any amount on the FarmLand Variable-Rate Mortgage (empty schedule) | never |
